contentBlocks.body: An upsert inserts a row if its key is new and updates the existing row if the key already exists. The naive version is two statements: SELECT to check, then INSERT or UPDATE. Under concurrency that is a race: two requests both see "not found" and both INSERT, giving you duplicate rows or a unique-key violation. The fix has two parts: a UNIQUE constraint (or primary key) on the natural key, and a single atomic statement.

contentBlocks.code:
-- PostgreSQL and SQLite: needs a UNIQUE constraint or PK on sku
INSERT INTO inventory (sku, qty)
VALUES ('MUG-01', 5)
ON CONFLICT (sku) DO UPDATE
  SET qty = inventory.qty + excluded.qty;   -- excluded = the row we tried to insert

-- MySQL
INSERT INTO inventory (sku, qty) VALUES ('MUG-01', 5)
ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE qty = qty + VALUES(qty);

contentBlocks.body: SQL Server also has MERGE, which can express an upsert in one statement, but MERGE on its own is not race-free: two sessions can still both decide to insert unless you add WITH (HOLDLOCK). Many teams prefer the explicit UPDATE-then-INSERT pattern above. EF Core has no built-in upsert; use raw SQL (or a library) when you need one, or catch the unique-violation exception and retry as an update.

Idempotent writes are what upserts are for: webhook handlers, sync jobs, and message consumers can receive the same event twice. An upsert keyed on the event id (or ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) makes the second delivery harmless.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Model `INSERT INTO inventory (sku, qty) VALUES (@sku, @qty) ON CONFLICT (sku) DO UPDATE SET qty = inventory.qty + excluded.qty`, run once per incoming row, in order. Existing rows keep their position; inserted rows are appended. Return { rows, inserted, updated } without mutating the input.
An API does `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tags WHERE name = @name` and INSERTs when the count is 0. Under load, duplicate tags appear. What is the correct fix?

choices: Add an index on name without making it unique
Run the SELECT twice before inserting
Add a UNIQUE constraint on name and use an atomic upsert (or catch the unique violation)
Cache the tag list in memory
payload.answer: Add a UNIQUE constraint on name and use an atomic upsert (or catch the unique violation)
payload.explanation: Check-then-insert is a race: both requests can pass the check before either inserts. Only the database can enforce uniqueness across concurrent sessions.

payload.text: INSERT INTO inventory (sku, qty) VALUES ('MUG-01', 5) ON CONFLICT (sku) DO ____ SET qty = excluded.qty;

knowledgeItems.prompt: In `ON CONFLICT (sku) DO UPDATE SET qty = inventory.qty + excluded.qty`, what is `excluded`?

choices: The existing row already in the table
A table of rows deleted by the statement
The row that was proposed for insertion but conflicted
payload.answer: The row that was proposed for insertion but conflicted
payload.explanation: excluded holds the values you tried to insert; the table name (inventory) refers to the existing row. SQL Server's MERGE uses a source alias for the same idea.
